**IN THE OPINION** of the artificial intelligence giant Anthropic, an AI model
should be permitted to [kill or seriously injure](https://cybernews.com/ai-
news/anthropic-50-people/) up to 50 people at a stretch.

A larger death toll than that, according to Anthropic's scrupulous moral
accounting, should prompt government regulators to block the release of a
model. Similarly, Anthropic contends that frontier AI should get to risk
causing as much as $1 _billion_ of damage before regulators intervene. All
that is contained in the draft of a bill Anthropic is pushing to shape the
long-awaited contours of an AI regulatory framework. "These are sensible
policies we believe Congress should act on," a company spokesperson
[told](https://www.politico.com/news/2026/10/16/anthropic-ai-safety-01124654)
_Politico_. Remember this the next time Anthropic positions itself as the
humane AI company.

Not that it's much comfort, but AI researchers, with astonishing casualness,
project that their products will cull far more than 50 people at a time. Last
month, Anthropic senior researcher Evan Hubinger tweeted that he considers AI
to have a greater than 10% chance of "[kill[ing] all humans… within the next
decade](https://x.com/EvanHub/status/2097497037956891126)." Hubinger was
reacting to Jacob Coxon, who announced he had quit Anthropic because it, and
rival OpenAI, were "[gambling with our
lives](https://x.com/hilbertspaess/status/2097476196791709843?s=20)." At least
Coxon, like Miles Dyson in 'Terminator 2'_,_ had the moral rigor to stop
committing harm; and Sarah Connor didn't even have to shoot him first. It is a
portrait of capitalist nihilism that people like Hubinger would continue to
develop a technology they believe might bring about extinction.

Coxon hastened to insist that AI researchers who make such predictions are not
engaged in a "marketing stunt." He said so because the handful of tech
oligarchs who control AI are thoroughly untrustworthy. They have [inflated an
AI bubble that threatens the U.S. economy](https://www.wheresyoured.at/the-
openai-bubble/?ref=ed-zitrons-wheres-your-ed-at-
newsletter&attribution_id=6a57981c3b2da400015e6338&attribution_type=post).
Many suspect that such apocalyptic forecasts are cynical, backdoor assurances
of AI potency that puff the bubble up ahead of long-expected IPOs. The
overwhelming majority of us, who have no visibility into the labs, have no
choice but to wonder whether those inside of them are building an extinction
machine or simply engaged in now-routine fraud. Maybe both?

All these should be considered clues.
